outlier: CineEntry is a clean, minimal online movie ticket booking web app built with Next.js, Prisma, BetterAuth, and ShadCN/UI.

recent_posts.title: Built a tool to generate structured mock data from SQL/CSV schemas
recent_posts.summary: GenTable AI is a newly launched tool that generates structured mock data from SQL, CSV, or JSON schemas. It lets users define custom columns, import existing schemas, and export ready-to-use CSV or JSON datasets instantly — aimed at developers who need realistic test data for dashboards and APIs without manual effort.

recent_posts.title: I Hand Crafted this and I think you should Check it Out!
recent_posts.summary: sayit wiki is an anonymous digital bulletin board where users can post notes without accounts or signups. Features include 16+ note styles, handwriting fonts, interactive masonry grid, likes/comments, auto-scroll mode, dark mode, keyboard shortcuts, UI sounds, and content moderation. Built to replicate the feel of a physical bulletin board with textures and animations.

recent_posts.title: TalentAI is a modern job board built with vibe coding — fast, clean, and developer-focused.
recent_posts.summary: TalentAI is an open-source job board platform for tech roles featuring AI-powered career insights via OpenAI, candidate application tracking, and recruiter dashboards. The stack includes Next.js, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Better Auth, and Tailwind with Shadcn UI components. Development was accelerated using Claude Code and Cursor AI coding assistants.

recent_posts.title: Using Copilot? Make Sure It’s Not Shipping Bugs to Prod
recent_posts.summary: AI coding assistants like Copilot can introduce security vulnerabilities, risky dependencies, and insecure pipeline changes that bypass traditional AppSec tools. A whitepaper examines security risks in AI-generated code, explains why SAST/SCA tools miss workflow issues, and provides practical approaches to maintain development speed while ensuring code safety.

recent_posts.title: At My Lowest Point as a Developer — I Need Advice
recent_posts.summary: A junior developer shares their struggle working as a sole developer after graduation, learning from poorly organized legacy code without mentorship. After seeing how experienced peers work, they're questioning their skills and career path, worried about AI replacing their abilities, and seeking advice on whether to stay or find a better learning environment.

recent_posts.title: WebGL shaders with Three.js in Nuxt
recent_posts.summary: WebGL and Three.js enable GPU-accelerated graphics and shader programming within Nuxt projects to create dynamic visual effects and immersive interfaces. By executing custom fragment and vertex shaders on the GPU, developers can build organic backgrounds and 3D experiences without performance penalties. Three.js abstracts low-level WebGL complexity into a JavaScript API, making advanced graphics techniques accessible for web applications. Integrating GPU-level graphics into modern web stacks has evolved from a niche technique to a key differentiator for creating expressive, interactive user experiences.

recent_posts.title: I built VBox - a polymorphic Vue.js component with a lightweight styling engine
recent_posts.summary: VBox is a polymorphic Vue.js component inspired by Chakra UI's Box that enables CSS properties as props. It features automatic vendor prefixing, responsive styles through breakpoints and container queries, light/dark themes, CSS property aliasing, and customizable theme tokens for colors, spacing, typography, and more.

recent_posts.title: The Infinite Software Crisis – Jake Nations, Netflix [Summary]
recent_posts.summary: AI code generation tools are creating an "Infinite Software Crisis" where developers ship code faster than they can understand it. Netflix engineer Jake Nations argues that AI makes coding "easy" but not "simple," leading to complexity spirals where technical debt gets perpetuated. He proposes a three-phase approach: compress context into research documents, create detailed implementation specs before coding, and only then let AI generate code. The key risk isn't bad code, but developers losing their architectural instincts and ability to recognize systemic problems.

recent_posts.title: New Threats in Open Source: Worms, AI-Driven Malware, and Trust Abuse
recent_posts.summary: The open source ecosystem faces escalating security threats including self-replicating worms like Shai-Hulud that spread across package registries, GlassWorm malware using invisible Unicode and blockchain command-and-control, AI-driven attacks with LLMs autonomously orchestrating exploitation chains, and massive spam campaigns abusing registry infrastructure. These threats transform every developer machine into a potential propagation point and require fundamental changes to supply chain defense strategies.

recent_posts.title: Thoughts on "Nine open source projects to watch in 2026"
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their experience with AI coding assistants, recommending Continue plugin with Ollama for VSCode, RooCode for scaffolding, and specific Qwen models. They suggest using MCP servers to keep LLMs current and advocate for local development with sufficient VRAM. Additional recommendations include self-hosting with Gitea for version control and package management, and comparing Turso with rqlite for distributed SQLite solutions.
